title: VF arrest, ROSC and STEMI
stem: A 58-year-old man complaining of chest pain collapses in the ED waiting area in front of the triage nurse. He has been brought into Resus 1 on a trolley. He is unresponsive. You lead the arrest team.

phases.title: Arrest
phases.goal: Confirm the arrest, call for help, start good CPR.

phases.title: Shock
phases.goal: Pads on during CPR and the first shock yourself: VF, so no SYNC.

phases.title: ALS
phases.goal: An airway with capnography, the drugs at the right shock, and the reversible causes. Then the rhythm check.

phases.title: After ROSC
phases.goal: Intubate, set the ventilator yourself for normocapnia, and hit the post-ROSC targets.

phases.title: The cause
phases.goal: The ECG after ROSC: what is it, and who needs to know? Antiplatelet from the cart.

review.text: When the first adrenaline goes in. Your notes follow AHA, which in some teaching gives adrenaline after the 2nd shock. RCUK and ERC give adrenaline 1 mg and amiodarone 300 mg after the 3rd shock. Know which algorithm your examiner expects.

notes:
Checked against Resuscitation Council UK 2025 adult ALS and post-resuscitation care guidelines (ERC 2025, ILCOR 2025), ESC 2023 ACS guidelines, and AHA 2025.

Shockable rhythm: shock as soon as possible (biphasic at least 150 J for the first shock; escalate if the device allows), resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes without a pulse check. Adrenaline 1 mg and amiodarone 300 mg after the third shock; adrenaline every 3–5 minutes (alternate loops); amiodarone 150 mg after the fifth shock (lidocaine 100 mg if amiodarone is not available). Place the apical pad directly below the armpit in the mid-axillary line; after three failed shocks consider a vector change to antero-posterior. RCUK 2025 does not recommend routine double sequential defibrillation.

Airway: basic airway or supraglottic airway is acceptable; intubate only if skilled (over 95% success within two attempts, pause under 5 s). Waveform capnography for every advanced airway.

Post-ROSC (RCUK/ERC–ESICM 2025): SpO2 94–98%, PaCO2 4.7–6.0 kPa, systolic over 100 or MAP 60–65 mmHg, actively prevent fever (37.5 °C or less) for 36–72 hours in comatose patients, treat seizures (levetiracetam or valproate), prognosticate at 72 hours or later. ST elevation after ROSC → emergency angiography and primary PCI.

Inferior STEMI: check right-sided leads (V4R) for right ventricular infarction; avoid nitrates and keep preload.

Your notes point to the AHA 2025 ACLS algorithm and highlights; the RCUK/ERC sequence here matches it on the scored points (AHA also gives adrenaline after the second shock in some teaching; RCUK after the third).

steps.hint: Confirm the arrest, call for help, start CPR.

opts.t: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, no carotid pulse in 10 seconds: call the arrest
Start compressions 30:2, 5–6 cm, 100–120/min

steps.label: Defibrillator
steps.hint: Pads on during CPR; VF: unsynchronised, 150 J or more; all clear.

opts.t: Pads on and shock
opts.performHint: CPR continues while you place the pads. VF: SYNC off, 150 J or more, CHARGE, ALL CLEAR, SHOCK.
mark: Correct pad placement without stopping CPR
All clear, oxygen away before the shock

steps.label: Team
steps.hint: Straight back on the chest; the next shocks at the 2-minute checks.

opts.t: Resume CPR at once for 2 minutes — no pulse check
opts.mark: Resumes CPR immediately after the shock

opts.t: Second and third shocks at each 2-minute check (still VF)
Stop CPR for a 10-second pulse check straight after each shock
opts.r: Resume compressions immediately; check rhythm at 2 minutes.

opts.t: Double sequential defibrillation after the first failed shock
opts.r: Not recommended routinely (RCUK 2025). Consider a vector change after three failed shocks.

opts.t: Supraglottic airway with waveform capnography; ventilate 10/min

steps.hint: After the third shock: adrenaline and amiodarone.

opts.r: In VF, shock first. Adrenaline comes after the third shock.
opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 1 mg IV before the first shock
opts.dose: 1 mg IV before the first shock

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 0.1 mg IV

opts.t: Amiodarone 300 mg IV

opts.t: Amiodarone 150 mg IV

steps.label: Rhythm check
steps.hint: After the drugs and the next cycle: rhythm, pulse, ETCO2.

opts.t: Rhythm check: organised rhythm, carotid pulse, ETCO2 has jumped
opts.r: Sinus rhythm at 96 with a pulse. ETCO2 rose sharply before the check.
opts.early: Keep going: CPR, shocks at the checks, the drugs.

opts.t: Think 4 Hs and 4 Ts aloud; likely coronary thrombosis
IV access; blood gas with potassium
opts.r: Nurse Tam: Gas: K 4.1, pH 7.18, lactate 6.

opts.t: Swap compressors every 2 minutes

steps.label: Intubate
steps.hint: GCS 3 after ROSC: secure the airway.

Airway.t: Intubate: laryngoscope, tube through the cords, cuff up, capnography
Airway.early: Not in the middle of CPR.

steps.label: Ventilator
steps.hint: Set it yourself: normocapnia after ROSC.

opts.t: Set the ventilator
opts.performHint: 80 kg, GCS 3 after ROSC. A controlled mode, 6–8 mL/kg, a normal rate for PaCO2 4.7–6.0 kPa. START.
mark: Oxygen, PEEP and a pressure limit

steps.label: After ROSC
steps.hint: Oxygen, pressure, temperature and glucose targets.

opts.t: Titrate oxygen to SpO2 94–98%
Systolic over 100 mmHg (MAP 60–65); fluids, then noradrenaline if needed
Prevent fever: 37.5 °C or less for 36–72 hours
Check glucose; arterial line
Cool him to 33 °C for 24 hours routinely
opts.r: Current guidance prevents fever; routine 33 °C cooling is not required.

opts.t: 100% oxygen for 24 hours to protect the brain
opts.r: Hyperoxia after arrest is harmful. Titrate to 94–98%.

steps.label: Investigations
steps.hint: 12-lead ECG now; right-sided leads for an inferior STEMI.

ECG.r: ST elevation in II, III and aVF (III more than II) with reciprocal depression in I and aVL.
ECG.mark: Identifies inferior STEMI with reciprocal change

ECG.r: 1 mm ST elevation in V4R: right ventricular involvement.

Other.r: ST elevation after ROSC does not wait for troponin.

opts.t: Cardiology: VF arrest, ROSC after 3 shocks, inferior STEMI with RV involvement — emergency primary PCI
opts.r: Cardiologist: Cath lab in 15 minutes. Give aspirin and heparin.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Antiplatelet for the STEMI; no nitrates with RV involvement.

opts.t: Aspirin 300 mg (NG or PR)
Aspirin 75 mg
opts.r: The loading dose is 300 mg (150–300 mg).
Right ventricular infarction is preload-dependent: nitrates can cause profound hypotension.
opts.t: GTN infusion for the chest pain
